## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
############################################################
# 0. Packages
############################################################
#install.packages(c("sf", "rnaturalearth", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "viridis"))
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(viridis)

############################################################
# 1. World polygons (admin-0 countries)
############################################################

world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
# Inspect the country name column
head(world$admin)

############################################################
# 2. Read your CSVs (adjust paths if needed)
############################################################

base_df <- read.csv("country_baseline_accessibility.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
p1_df   <- read.csv("country_vulnerability_p1.csv",  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
p5_df   <- read.csv("country_vulnerability_p5.csv",  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
p10_df  <- read.csv("country_vulnerability_p10.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Each of these has at least: country, AC_base, EAL_C_hat, rEAL_C_hat

############################################################
# 3. Country name mapping
############################################################

# Map from your 'country' names to rnaturalearth's 'admin' names
name_map <- c(
  "United States"       = "United States of America",
  "Cote d'Ivoire"       = "Côte d'Ivoire",
  "Congo (Brazzaville)" = "Republic of the Congo",
  "Congo (Kinshasa)"    = "Democratic Republic of the Congo",
  "Russia"              = "Russia",
  "Bolivia"             = "Bolivia (Plurinational State of)",
  "Venezuela"           = "Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of)"
  # Add more here if needed when you see unmatched countries
)

# Helper to add a column with the join key
add_admin_join <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      admin_join = dplyr::recode(country, !!!name_map, .default = country)
    )
}

base_df  <- add_admin_join(base_df)
p1_df    <- add_admin_join(p1_df)
p5_df    <- add_admin_join(p5_df)
p10_df   <- add_admin_join(p10_df)

############################################################
# 4. Helper to join and plot a choropleth
############################################################

join_world <- function(metric_df) {
  world %>%
    left_join(metric_df, by = c("admin" = "admin_join"))
}

plot_choropleth <- function(world_metric, value_col, title, na_color = "grey90") {
  ggplot(world_metric) +
    geom_sf(aes_string(fill = value_col), color = NA) +
    scale_fill_viridis(option = "C", na.value = na_color) +
    labs(fill = value_col, title = title) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text = element_blank(),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    )
}

############################################################
# 5. Baseline accessibility map
############################################################

world_base <- join_world(base_df)

# Quick check: which countries are unmatched (NA AC_base)?
unmatched_base <- world_base %>%
  filter(!is.na(admin) & is.na(AC_base)) %>%
  select(admin) %>%
  distinct()
head(unmatched_base)  # use this to refine name_map if needed

# Plot baseline AC(G)
plot_choropleth(world_base, "AC_base", "Baseline country accessibility AC(G)")

############################################################
# 6. Vulnerability maps for p = 1%, 5%, 10%
############################################################

world_p1  <- join_world(p1_df)
world_p5  <- join_world(p5_df)
world_p10 <- join_world(p10_df)

# Optionally set a common scale for rEAL across p to make maps comparable
all_rEAL <- c(world_p1$rEAL_C_hat, world_p5$rEAL_C_hat, world_p10$rEAL_C_hat)
global_min <- min(all_rEAL, na.rm = TRUE)
global_max <- max(all_rEAL, na.rm = TRUE)

plot_choropleth(
  world_p1,
  "rEAL_C_hat",
  "Relative expected accessibility loss rEAL^C (p = 1%)"
) + scale_fill_viridis(option = "C", limits = c(global_min, global_max), na.value = "grey90")

plot_choropleth(
  world_p5,
  "rEAL_C_hat",
  "Relative expected accessibility loss rEAL^C (p = 5%)"
) + scale_fill_viridis(option = "C", limits = c(global_min, global_max), na.value = "grey90")

plot_choropleth(
  world_p10,
  "rEAL_C_hat",
  "Relative expected accessibility loss rEAL^C (p = 10%)"
) + scale_fill_viridis(option = "C", limits = c(global_min, global_max), na.value = "grey90")

```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
############################################################
# Packages
############################################################
#install.packages(c("ergm", "network", "geosphere", "dplyr"))
library(ergm)
library(network)
library(geosphere)
library(dplyr)

############################################################
# 1. Read node and edge data
############################################################

nodes <- read.csv("airports_cc_nodes.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
edges <- read.csv("airports_cc_edges.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

n <- nrow(nodes)

# Map airport_id -> 1..n
id_map <- setNames(seq_len(n), nodes$airport_id)

edges_i <- id_map[as.character(edges$from_airport_id)]
edges_j <- id_map[as.character(edges$to_airport_id)]

g <- network.initialize(n, directed = FALSE)
add.edges(g, tail = edges_i, head = edges_j)

# Attach attributes
set.vertex.attribute(g, "airport_id", nodes$airport_id)
set.vertex.attribute(g, "country",    nodes$country)
set.vertex.attribute(g, "name",       nodes$name)
set.vertex.attribute(g, "city",       nodes$city)

# Coordinates matrix (lon, lat) for distance
coords <- as.matrix(nodes[, c("longitude", "latitude")])

############################################################
# 3. Edge covariate: log distance
############################################################

# Great-circle distances (in meters)
dist_mat_m <- distm(coords, fun = distHaversine)
# Convert to km and transform
dist_mat_km <- dist_mat_m / 1000
log_dist <- log(dist_mat_km + 1)  # add 1 to avoid log(0)

# Ensure it's a standard matrix with correct dim
log_dist <- matrix(log_dist, nrow = n, ncol = n)

############################################################
# Quick checks
############################################################

g
summary(g)
table(get.vertex.attribute(g, "country"))[1:10]

```

```{r}
############################################################
# 4. Fit ERGM
############################################################

set.seed(123)

model1 <- ergm(
  g ~ edges +
        gwesp(0.5, fixed = TRUE) +
        nodematch("country", diff = FALSE) +
        edgecov(log_dist),
  control = control.ergm(
    MCMLE.maxit   = 20,
    MCMC.interval = 1e4,
    MCMC.burnin   = 5e4,
    MCMC.samplesize = 1e4
  )
)

summary(model1)

```

```{r}
############################################################
# 5. GOF diagnostics
############################################################

gof1 <- gof(model1, GOF = ~ degree + distance + espartners + triadcensus)
print(gof1)
plot(gof1)

```

```{r}
# Example extension with degree term:
model2 <- ergm(
  g ~ edges +
        gwesp(0.5, fixed = TRUE) +
        nodematch("country", diff = FALSE) +
        edgecov(log_dist) +
        gwdegree(0.5, fixed = TRUE),
  control = control.ergm(
    MCMLE.maxit   = 20,
    MCMC.interval = 1e4,
    MCMC.burnin   = 5e4,
    MCMC.samplesize = 1e4
  )
)

summary(model2)
gof2 <- gof(model2, GOF = ~ degree + distance + espartners + triadcensus)
plot(gof2)

```
```{r}
############################################################
# A1. Simulate nsim networks from the ERGM
############################################################
library(ergm)
library(network)

set.seed(123)

nsim <- 50   # increase later if runtime is OK

sim_list <- simulate(
  model1,
  nsim      = nsim,
  output    = "network",
  control   = control.simulate.ergm(MCMC.interval = 10000)
)

############################################################
# A2. Export each simulated network as an edgelist with airport_id labels
############################################################

# Vertex labels from the original network (airport IDs)
airport_ids <- get.vertex.attribute(g, "airport_id")

for (s in seq_len(nsim)) {
  g_s <- sim_list[[s]]

  el <- as.edgelist(g_s)  # matrix of vertex indices (i,j)
  if (is.null(el) || nrow(el) == 0) {
    # If a simulated network has no edges (unlikely), skip
    next
  }

  df_el <- data.frame(
    from_airport_id = airport_ids[el[, 1]],
    to_airport_id   = airport_ids[el[, 2]]
  )

  fname <- sprintf("ergm_sim_edges_%02d.csv", s)
  write.csv(df_el, fname, row.names = FALSE)
  cat("Wrote", fname, "with", nrow(df_el), "edges\n")
}

```
